issues.failure_explanation: As written, \xi_t=t\sqrt{\xi_1} is not the diffusion scaling used by the scheme and is incompatible with non-degenerate independent increments: increments would all be scalar multiples of the same \sqrt{\xi_1}. The PIDE/Feynman-Kac discussion and the h^{1/2} increments require \xi_t\overset d=\sqrt{t}\,\xi_1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed scaling by the standard diffusion scaling \xi_t\overset d=\sqrt{t}\,\xi_1 (or \xi_t=\sqrt{t}\xi_1 in law) and correct the one occurrence of t\sqrt{\xi_1}.
issues.overall_effect: The recalled scaling of the nonlinear Lévy process is false as written, undermining the stated connection between the PIDE, the scheme, and the robust limit theorem until corrected.
issues.title: Wrong diffusion scaling in the nonlinear Lévy process
issues.why_classification: The correction is a single forced scaling fix; after it, the proofs and rates can proceed as written without new architecture or loss of advertised rate.

issues.failure_explanation: Since \tau\in(-\varepsilon^2,0), the convolution uses v(t-\tau) with t-\tau>t, i.e. future values. The PIDE solution u and u_h are only defined on [0,1], so u^\varepsilon is not well-defined for t near 1 unless an unspecified extension is introduced. The standard parabolic regularization must be backward in time.

Thus the displayed inequality is not justified.

issues.overall_effect: The lower error bound in the main theorem, and the lower side of the robust-limit rate, are not proved as stated. The convergence rate survives after adjusting constants, but the exact stated barrier is unsupported.

The final conclusion follows only if that displayed exponent is replaced by 1/2 or the \delta/\alpha estimate is independently proved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the smallest H\"{o}lder conjugate exponent $q_1$ satisfies $q_1 \geq \frac{3}{2}$. This yields the lower bound for $\delta$, given by $\delta > \alpha \frac{q_1}{2} \geq \frac{3}{4}\alpha$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof fixes q_1=3/2 and uses the interpolation estimate with factor \|D_x\omega\|^{q_1-\delta}. This is not justified when \delta>q_1=3/2, even though Assumption (v) allows \delta up to \alpha<2. For \alpha>3/2 the advertised \delta-range and the rate obtained by letting \delta\to\alpha are therefore not supported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict \delta to \delta<\min(\alpha,3/2) in Assumption (v) and re-optimize the rate, or add a new interpolation/moment argument justifying the case \delta>3/2. The source-supported repair is the restriction plus reoptimization.
issues.overall_effect: The consistency lemma is not proved for the full assumed range of \delta. Consequently the main error bounds and the robust-limit rates that use the \delta-dependent term are only supported for a smaller \delta, with a worse rate when \alpha>3/2.
issues.title: Consistency estimate only proved for \delta \le 3/2
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained, but it excludes part of the advertised \delta-regime and materially weakens the rate for \alpha>3/2 (e.g. the \delta-term is bounded by (2-\alpha)/(4\alpha) rather than its supremum 1/(4\alpha+6) as \delta\to\alpha).
